title.en: Host a guest, avoid the clash
title.es: Recibir a un invitado sin choques

es: Recibir a un invitado extranjero: explicar dos costumbres con matices, aclarar un malentendido con tacto y responder a una pregunta incómoda.

vocabulary.es: no quise decir, no era mi intención

teaching.en: Please feel at home: a guest who is afraid to open the fridge will never relax, however kind the welcome.
teaching.es: Siéntete como en casa: un invitado que tiene miedo de abrir la nevera nunca se relajará, por amable que sea la bienvenida.
teaching.explanationEs: Feel at home es una bienvenida cálida que da permiso al invitado.
segments: Please feel at home: a guest who is afraid to
open the fridge will never relax, however kind the welcome.
teaching.audioText: Please feel at home: a guest who is afraid to open the fridge will never relax, however kind the welcome.

teaching.en: If a misunderstanding has spoiled the evening, apologise briefly and tactfully, without blaming the guest.
teaching.es: Si un malentendido ha estropeado la velada, discúlpate con brevedad y con tacto, sin culpar al invitado.
teaching.explanationEs: Apologise reconoce un fallo sin dramatizar; se dice apologise for…
segments: If a misunderstanding has spoiled the evening, apologise
briefly and tactfully, without blaming the guest.
teaching.audioText: If a misunderstanding has spoiled the evening, apologise briefly and tactfully, without blaming the guest.

teaching.en: Let me clarify: we did not mean to ignore you when we started eating, because in our house nobody waits after seven.
teaching.es: Déjame aclarar: no queríamos ignorarte cuando empezamos a comer, porque en nuestra casa nadie espera después de las siete.
teaching.explanationEs: Clarify + did not mean: aclara la intención sin culpar a nadie.
segments: Let me clarify: we did not mean to ignore you when
we started eating, because in our house nobody waits after seven.
teaching.audioText: Let me clarify: we did not mean to ignore you when we started eating, because in our house nobody waits after seven.

teaching.en: When the guest asks an awkward question, say “Good question” and tread carefully: answer honestly, but without absolute words.
teaching.es: Cuando el invitado hace una pregunta incómoda, di «Buena pregunta» y ve con cuidado: responde con honestidad, pero sin palabras absolutas.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconocer lo delicado y responder sin «siempre» ni «nunca» evita una discusión.
segments: When the guest asks an awkward question, say “Good question”
and tread carefully: answer honestly, but without absolute words.
teaching.audioText: When the guest asks an awkward question, say “Good question” and tread carefully: answer honestly, but without absolute words.

teaching.en: To clear the air after a clash, set the record straight about your custom and invite the guest to ask anything.
teaching.es: Para despejar el ambiente tras un choque, aclara las cosas sobre tu costumbre e invita al invitado a preguntar lo que quiera.
teaching.explanationEs: Clear the air y set the record straight buscan reparar, no ganar.
segments: To clear the air after a clash, set the record straight
about your custom and invite the guest to ask anything.
teaching.audioText: To clear the air after a clash, set the record straight about your custom and invite the guest to ask anything.

teaching.en: “No offence” is a softener for criticism, so use it sparingly, and never after an awkward remark that has already hurt someone.
teaching.es: «Sin ofender» suaviza una crítica, así que úsalo con moderación y nunca tras un comentario incómodo que ya ha herido a alguien.
teaching.explanationEs: No offence no borra una ofensa: solo suaviza lo que aún no se ha dicho.

prompt.es: Lee el intercambio: ¿por qué es diplomática la respuesta de Sara?

choices.text: It avoids the question by changing the subject quickly.
It admits that the family is unfriendly to every guest.
It welcomes the question and avoids absolute words.

feedback.es: Sara reconoce la pregunta con «Good question!» y responde con by and large y una razón concreta, sin absolutos ni evasivas.

hint.es: Fíjate en cómo empieza su respuesta y en las palabras que evita.

origin.text: Carlos, a guest from abroad, asks his hosts why nobody talks during dinner. Sara smiles and answers, “Good question! By and large we talk a lot, but tonight we were all very tired.” Carlos laughs, and the silence disappears.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ana preparó té para despejar el ambiente.»

feedback.es: Clear the air es la expresión fija para disipar la tensión tras una discusión o un malentendido.

origin.text: After the argument at dinner, nobody wanted to speak first, so Ana made tea to clear the ___ between them and offer a fresh start.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión del anfitrión con su función.

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple un papel distinto al recibir a un invitado: aclarar, suavizar, acoger y responder con tacto.

hint.es: Piensa en el orden de una visita: bienvenida, malentendido, pregunta.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué hizo especialmente bien el padre al contestar a la invitada?

choices.text: He explained the habit but insisted that the guest must follow it.
He explained the habit and offered to adapt it if the guest preferred.
He offered to change the habit without explaining why it exists.
He apologised for the habit and promised to abandon it for good.

feedback.es: Reconoce la pregunta, describe el hábito con «tend to» y se ofrece a adaptarlo: así la invitada se siente en casa.

origin.audio: Our guest from Canada arrived on Friday and asked why we never eat before eight. My father said, “Good question. Most families here tend to eat late, but it is only a habit, and we can eat earlier if you prefer.” The guest looked relieved. She said later that nobody had ever answered her so kindly, and that she felt at home by the end of the evening.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje: ¿qué busca quien lo escribe?

choices.text: To excuse the family by proving that the guest was in the wrong.
To ask the guest to follow the customs of the house from now on.
To clear the air by explaining the custom kindly.
To cancel the invitation politely without saying so.

feedback.es: Se disculpa, explica la costumbre (la cocinera come la última) y deja la puerta abierta a más preguntas, sin culpar al invitado.

origin.text: I apologise for what happened at dinner. We did not mean to leave you out; in our house the cook eats last and the guests start first, so we assumed that you would begin. Please tell me if anything else surprises you.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por favor, siéntete como en casa y pregúntame lo que quieras.»

answer.text: Please feel at home and ask me anything

feedback.es: Feel at home es una expresión fija; ask me anything invita al invitado a preguntar sin reservas.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿cómo arregla la familia la situación con Jamal?

choices.text: By asking Jamal to explain why he had not slept well that night.
By removing the house rules and inviting him to write his own list.
By telling Jamal politely that a second blanket was not really needed.
By saying sorry for the joke, making clear the list was no order and giving him a blanket.

feedback.es: La familia se disculpa por la broma, aclara que la lista no era una orden y ofrece la manta sin comentarios: reparar sin culpar.

origin.audio: When Jamal, an exchange student from Kenya, came to stay with us, my mother gave him a list of house rules, which was the first mistake. The second was my father's joke that only tourists ask for a second blanket. Jamal smiled politely, but the next morning he looked tired. My mother, who reads faces well, took me aside and suggested that we apologise for the joke, clarify that the list was not an order, and offer a blanket without comment. At breakfast my father said, with a smile, that he had been a bad host and a worse performer. Jamal laughed, accepted the blanket, and asked whether the house rules included the recipe for my mother's bread.

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca quien escribe al responder así a la pregunta incómoda de Hana?

choices.text: To reply frankly to a difficult question, limited to what the writer knows.
To avoid the question by praising the families the writer knows.
To prove that every family in the town is quieter than Hana's.
To apologise because the writer's family is so different from Hana's.

feedback.es: Acota («only speak for the families I know»), matiza con «many» y «tend to» y explica sin disculparse: una respuesta sincera y sin absolutos.

origin.text: Dear Hana, you asked whether all the families in our town are as quiet as mine. It is a good question, and I should say first that I can only speak for the families I know. Many of them tend to be reserved at dinner, but others are noisy, particularly on Sundays. Please do not take our quiet as a sign that we are cold; it is simply how we were brought up.

prompt.es: Completa: «Déjame aclarar lo que pasó anoche.»

feedback.es: Set the record straight es la expresión fija para corregir una impresión equivocada.

origin.text: I did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you, so let me set the record ___ about what happened last night.

prompt.es: Da la bienvenida a tu invitado, aclara y responde con tacto (200–260 palabras).

answer.text: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? It is a fair thing to wonder, and I will try to answer tactfully. Some families are quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first, whereas in your country people seem to talk more. Neither way is better, and it is only a habit; nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city. No offence if we are quiet again on Sunday: my grandmother cooks, and we tend to listen to her stories.
accepted: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? It is a fair thing to wonder, and I will try to answer tactfully. Some families are quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first, whereas in your country people seem to talk more. Neither way is better, and it is only a habit; nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city. No offence if we are quiet again on Sunday: my grandmother cooks, and we tend to listen to her stories.

Hello, Hana, make yourself at home! As a rule, my family has breakfast together at eight, and we tend to be quiet because we are still sleepy. Let me explain something about this morning: we did not mean to ignore you when we stayed silent. I am sorry, because I should have told you about our custom. That is a fair question: why is nobody talking at the table? In some houses people talk a lot at breakfast, whereas in ours we like silence and coffee first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. At lunch we will talk as much as you like, and I promise to ask you about your country and your family. I hope that you will feel at ease with us very soon.

feedback.es: El texto da la bienvenida, explica costumbres con matices, aclara el malentendido sin culpar y responde con tacto a la pregunta.

origin.text: Tu invitado Carlos llega de otro país. Escribe en inglés: da la bienvenida, explica dos costumbres con matices (tend to, by and large), aclara un malentendido (por ejemplo, que empezaron a comer sin él) con Let me clarify… y responde con tacto a su pregunta: «Why do you not talk more at dinner?».

evidenceGroups: let me set the record straight

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la actitud de quien escribe ante los invitados de otros países?

choices.text: Guests should accept every habit of the host without asking.
Open explanation and questions are better than guessing what offends.
It is wiser to avoid inviting people from other countries.
Hosts should leave every guest alone to avoid any problem.

feedback.es: Ya no adivina qué ofende: explica sus hábitos y pregunta por los del invitado, una estrategia sin coste que evita casi todo el daño.

origin.text: Hosting a foreigner taught me that politeness has no universal grammar. Some guests want to be left alone; others think that being left alone means being ignored. I used to worry that every choice would offend someone. Now I explain my habits openly and ask about theirs, which costs nothing and avoids most of the damage.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame aclarar lo que no quisimos decir.»

answer.text: Let me clarify what we did not mean to say

feedback.es: Let me clarify + what + oración: aclara la intención sin culpar a nadie.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje del invitado: ¿qué quiere transmitir?

choices.text: That the guest was offended by the question about the guest's country.
That the guest regrets having accepted the invitation.
That the guest enjoyed the evening and feels comfortable with the family.
That the guest thinks the family talks too much at dinner.

feedback.es: Agradece la velada, resta importancia a su respuesta larga y cierra con un proverbio que muestra que se siente a gusto.

origin.audio: Thank you for the lovely evening. Your question about my country was not awkward at all, although I am afraid my answer was too long. Please tell me if I talk too much. Back home we say that a guest who is shy at the start is a guest who will be very happy in the end.
